clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old male nurse practitioner presented with a 6-year history of disabling bilateral upper extremity pruritus localized to the C6 dermatome (biceps region), associated with constant bilateral neck pain and intermittent burning/paresthesias. Symptoms were mechanical in nature, worsening with neck lateral rotation and reaching, temporarily relieved by epidural steroid injections, and disrupting sleep. Extensive prior evaluation by dermatology, rheumatology, neurology, and psychiatry had excluded primary dermatologic disease, peripheral neuropathy, and psychiatric etiologies. Physical examination revealed grossly normal skin in the affected areas (ruling out primary dermatologic pathology) and positive Spurling signs bilaterally indicating cervical nerve root irritation, with preserved motor strength (5/5), symmetric reflexes (2+), and intact sensation in the upper extremities. Cervical spine MRI demonstrated multilevel spondylotic pathology with spinal stenosis and early cord flattening at C3-4 and C4-5, and multilevel foraminal stenosis from C3 to C7, providing an anatomical correlate for the C6 radicular symptoms. After failure of extensive conservative multimodal therapies, the patient underwent anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) from C3 to C7 without complication. At four months postoperatively, he reported 95% improvement in preoperative symptoms with resolution of pain and only occasional residual pruritus, confirming the cervical spine pathology as the etiology of the neuropathic itch.
